title: Control how fast Courier sends to your providers
summary: Set a send rate limit on any Courier provider, like Amazon SES or Twilio. Send at any rate, and Courier queues the rest and sends at the rate you set.
body_markdown:
Notifications rarely go out at an even rate. A product announcement goes to your whole user base at once. A nightly job finishes and produces thousands of reminders in a few seconds. A busy afternoon of signups turns into a spike of welcome emails.


Courier takes all of that as fast as you send it. The providers behind Courier each have their own limit on how fast you can send, and no two are the same. Amazon SES gives each account a maximum send rate. SMS providers limit each sender number. Even two accounts with the same provider can have different limits.


You shouldn't have to keep track of any of that in your code, and now you don't. Tell Courier how fast each provider can take notifications with a **send rate limit** , and Courier handles the rest. You send as fast as you want, and each provider gets them at the rate it allows.


## How it works


A send rate limit sets how many notifications Courier sends to one provider per second, minute, or hour. From then on, Courier accepts every send you make. Anything over the limit is queued, not dropped, and goes out to the provider at the rate you set. You don't batch sends yourself, and you don't write retry logic for a provider that's pushing back.


Each provider you connect has its own limit, so two SES accounts can run at two different rates. Test and Production are set separately too. Your Test environment can match an[Amazon SES](https://www.courier.com/docs/integrations/email/aws-ses) sandbox account while Production uses your full sending rate.


If you don't set a limit, nothing changes. Courier sends to the provider as fast as it can, the same as it always has.


## Setting a provider send rate limit


In the Courier console, open Integrations, click the provider, and click **Settings** . Enter a number in **Send Rate Limit** , pick second, minute, or hour under **Per** , and the limit applies within 60 seconds. Clear the field to remove it.


If you manage providers in code, send only` rate_limit` with` PATCH /providers/{id}` . Your credentials and every other setting stay as they are.


Terminal


```text
curl   -X   PATCH "https://api.courier.com/providers/  $PROVIDER_CONFIG_ID "   \
-H   "Authorization: Bearer   $COURIER_API_KEY "   \
-H   "Content-Type: application/json"   \
-d   '{ "settings": { "rate_limit": { "rate": 10, "period": "second" } } }'
```


To remove the limit, send` "rate_limit": null` the same way.


Send rate limits are available on every provider today. Read the[docs](https://www.courier.com/docs/integrations/send-rate-limits) for the details, or open your provider's settings in the[Integrations](https://app.courier.com/integrations) section of the Courier console and set one.


## Frequently asked questions


### Does Courier drop sends that go over the rate limit?


Courier queues sends that go over the limit and sends them to the provider at the rate you set. None are dropped.


### What happens if I don't set a send rate limit?


Courier sends to the provider as fast as it can, the same as before.


### Is the send rate limit set per provider or per workspace?


Each provider you connect in Courier has its own send rate limit, and Test and Production are set separately.


### How do I stay under my Amazon SES maximum send rate?


Set a send rate limit on your Amazon SES provider in Courier that matches your account's maximum send rate. Courier queues anything above it and sends to SES at that rate.


### Can I set a send rate limit with the Courier API?


The Courier API sets it as` rate_limit` in a provider's` settings` . Send it with` PATCH /providers/{id}` to change only the limit, or include it when you create a provider with` POST /providers` . It takes a` rate` and a` period` of` second` ,` minute` , or` hour` .
